paper_sections.title: Estimating effective connectivity in Alzheimer's disease progression: A dynamic causal modeling study

description.value: The study examined resting-state effective connectivity among default mode, salience, and central executive network regions across cognitively normal, EMCI, LMCI, and Alzheimer's disease groups, and tested whether connectivity predicted MMSE and CDR scores.

design.value: A retrospective longitudinal resting-state fMRI study using publicly available ADNI-2 data from four clinically defined groups, with subject-level dynamic causal modeling, group-level parametric empirical Bayes and Bayesian model reduction, ANOVA comparisons, and linear regression of connectivity against cognitive scores.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained. During the fMRI scans, all participants were instructed to keep their eyes open and relax.

instructions.value: Keep their eyes open and relax.

description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence. Each series has 140 volumes, and each volume consists of 48 slices of image matrices with dimensions 64 × 64 with voxel size of 3.31 × 3.31 × 3.31 mm3.
T1 image used for unified segmentation during spatial normalization to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

The preprocessing was carried out using SPM 12 and RESTplus toolkits. The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded, and the remaining 130 volumes were slice-time corrected, followed by regression of head motion parameters, realignment for head movement, and spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to MNI space.

steps.value: The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded from analysis to allow for participant's stabilization and magnetic field equilibration.
The remaining 130 volumes were corrected for the staggered order of slice acquisition that was used during echo-planar scanning.
Spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

model_settings.value: DCM comprised a neuronal model and an observation model. The neuronal model used ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + Cu + v, with intrinsic connectivity, extrinsic connectivity, and input parameters; for resting state, stimulus u was usually set to zero. The observation model was the generalized BOLD signal model in which blood volume and deoxyhemoglobin content affect the observed BOLD signal. ROI activity was summarized by extracting time series from all voxels within an 8-mm-radius sphere around each associated MNI coordinate.

PEB was used to infer connectivity strengths for the four subject groups. A parameter vector was sampled from a prior distribution, a random effect was added for the subject, data were generated using the DCM with observation noise, and connection strengths were selected by thresholding the likelihood.
BMR was used to control the switching on and off of each connection, calculate the likelihood with the connection's presence and absence, and estimate the parameter to infer the connectivity pattern.
The connectivity strengths for each subject group were compared using analysis of variance (ANOVA). Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

A linear regression analysis was carried out to test if effective connectivity between regions could predict subjects' cognitive scores. For MMSE, forward step-wise linear regression was used. For CDR, both forward and backward connections between L-dlPFC and mPFC were predictive of the score.
